text:
Predicates:
Schedule(x) ::: x schedules a meeting with their customers.
Appear(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
Lunch(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
Home(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
Remote(x) ::: x is working remotely from home.
Country(x) ::: x is in other countries.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
Premises:
∀x ((Employee(x) ∧ Schedule(x)) → Appear(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (Lunch(x) → Schedule(x)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Lunch(x) ⊕ Home(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
Home(x) → Remote(x) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (Country(x) → Remote(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬Remote(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ Appear(james)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ Appear(james)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
¬Lunch(james) ::: James does not have lunch in the company.
